Gobhila
------------------------------------------
Gobhila was an ancient sage who belonged to the group of followers of the Sāmaveda. Nothing is known of him. Adherents of the Kauthuma and the Rāṇāyaṇīya schools of the Sāmaveda consider his works as highly authoritative.
Three works are attributed to him: Gobhila गृह्यसूत्रस्, गोभिल Smṛti and Gobhila Śrāddhakalpa.
The Gobhila Gṛhyasūtras, the text of which has been fully recovered, has four main sections called ‘prapāṭhakas’. Each prapāṭhaka is divided into ‘kaṇḍikās’ (chapters) and the kaṇḍikās have indi-vidual sūtras or aphorisms. The total number of sūtras is 1089 accommodated in 39 kaṇḍikās.
It has three commentaries by: भट्ट नारायण, Yaśodhara and an unknown author (the commentary itself being called Saralā).
Being a gṛhyasūtra work, it naturally deals with the rites and rituals connected with the life of a गृहस्थ or a householder. The topics dealt with include some sacrifices like पितृयज्ञ, Pārvaṇayajña, Aṣṭakāyajña, Āgrahāyaṇīyajña, the pañca-महायज्ञस् (five daily sacrifices) and 13 सṁस्कारस् like जातकर्म, उपनयन, समावर्तन, विवाह and अन्त्येष्टि.
The Gobhilasmṛti has been identified with the Karmapradīpa of कात्यायन (4th cent. A. D.). It deals with the usual topics found in the smṛtis and धर्मशास्त्रस् like आचार (daily routine and behaviour), the सन्ध्या ritual, जप of Vedic mantras, śrāddha, अशौच, तर्पण and so on.
The work Gobhilīya Śrāddhakalpa has not been found till now. Portions from it have been quoted in the works of other authors like रघुनन्दन (A. D. 1510-1580) in his Śrāddhatattva.
